segments.title: essence and mistaken perception
segments.note: PROVISIONAL machine alignment reconciled by Codex from independent Tibetan-first and English-first proposals; no human semantic acceptance. rang gi licenses their and kyis the contextual means/essence expression in. The first grub owns existed and the second grub owns the separate whole word exist. gnas lugs/independent reality and ngo bo nyid/very essence are glossary attestations. 'khrul pa is a nominal error/delusion here, rendered contextually as the whole mistaken states of mind; its HGM entry attests mistaken and delusion, not that exact full phrase. Initial na owns If and later na owns when. Supplied things, they, you, your, finally and auxiliary wording stay unpaired. The temporal de'i tshe/If this were so recast and the expanded introductory formula are omitted; don retains meaning. ldog owns disappear and mi owns never. gsal du 'gro dgos kyi and although they should have remain unresolved and omitted, not nulled: the glossary's HGM25759 explicitly attests gsal du 'gro/disappear at HTG2016 tier, while ILL's full corresponding passage uses brought-to-light wording. The proposed categorical English erratum is refuted for insufficient certainty given this actual attestation and the possible argument-level elliptical recast; neither interpretation is substituted into the source. All source text remains verbatim.
